decisionMemo.businessProblem: A 200+ unit company-operated QSR chain with ~$850M of system revenue (AUV ~$4.25M) is experiencing declining unit-level profitability despite stable system revenue. Same-store sales are flat (0% YoY): the operator took +2% of menu price, but it was fully offset by a -2% traffic decline, so there is no top-line offset to absorb cost inflation. Meanwhile food & paper (COGS) cost inflation ran +8% and labor cost inflation ran +10% (rising minimum wages plus scheduling/overtime pressure). As a result, food & paper rose from 28.0% to 30.0% of sales and labor rose from 30.0% to 32.0% of sales, while occupancy (9%) and other opex (14%) held. Restaurant-level EBITDA margin therefore fell from 19.0% to 15.0%, a 400 bps decline (~$170k of EBITDA per unit, ~$34M across the system). The core challenge: Is this a pricing-structure error (the menu is mispriced), a demand-forecasting/traffic problem (the chain mis-read demand), or a four-wall unit-economics breakdown (the per-unit cost of output has outrun sustainable contribution)? Pricing power is capped by competition and value-menu commitments; cutting labor risks slowing service and further eroding traffic and SSS. The CEO must decide—before a covenant-relevant lender/franchise review in 60-90 days—whether to re-engineer the unit model, take additional price, or slow new-unit growth.
